key_insight: EEG-Xplain provides a unified attribution framework to interpret black-box EEG foundation models by linking model decisions to spatial, temporal, and spectral EEG patterns.
engineering_relevance: It gives researchers a standardized way to assess interpretability, reliability, and physiological plausibility across heterogeneous EEG architectures before clinical deployment.
method: Uses gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based explanations.
Maps critical channels, time segments, and frequency-band contributions.
Adds population-level reliability checks with AOPC and cross-method consistency.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Mumtaz2016 and TUAB show explanations aligned with known neurophysiological markers while also revealing artifact and spurious-pattern dependencies.
watch_item: LLM-generated reports can improve usability, but attribution quality still depends on robust explanation methods and careful control for artifacts.
paper_title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models
